data.gender_notes: Iyappa is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Iyappa is the son of Lord Shiva and goddess Parvathi. He is considered the god of war, strength and courage. The name Iyappa carries the meaning “God of War” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Iyappa usually hope their child will grow to embody god of war and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Iyappa belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of War.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iyappa total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Iyappa is deeply revered in the Hindu culture, particularly in South India and parts of Sri Lanka. He is known as Lord Ayyappan, and legends state that he appeared to assist the wise saint Vangsahar in the contested battle for his wife Malayali, offering him his divine strength and knowledge. This event led to the deification of Iyappa, who became the protective deity of the town of Sabarimala and the surrounding areas. Many rituals, including the annual pilgrimage to Sabarimala temple by millions of devotees, are dedicated to Iyappa, highlighting his significance and influence on Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Iyappa represents the divine qualities of strength, courage, and determination. In Hindu mythology, the god is believed to have displayed immense patience, devotion, and self-discipline as he offered his services to Lord Shiva, despite facing numerous challenges. Iyappa is thus worshipped by Hindus as an embodiment of perseverance, and is considered a symbol of overcoming obstacles and staying strong in the face of adversity. Devotees believe that invoking the blessings of Lord Iyappa can provide them with the inner strength they need to face difficult situations and overcome personal challenges.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Iyappa, also known as Ayyappan, is a revered Hindu deity in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Symbolizing purity, strength, and devotion, Iyappa is believed to protect the devotees from dangers and fulfill their wishes. He is an embodiment of Lord Shiva and Vishnu, representing the unity of diverse deities in Hinduism.

vedic_reference.root_origin: Sanskrit roots ईश् (ish) and अप (ap) meaning 'lord' and 'hunt' respectively
vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas, Upanishads, or other scriptures, but name of a popular deity in South India.

historical_references.reference: Iyappa is believed to be an incarnation of the Hindu god Ayyappan, who is the protector of Sabarimala temple in Kerala, India. Ayyappan is the son of Shiva and Mohini, the divine enchantress. Iyappa is a popular deity among Hindus, particularly in the southern states of India.

The legend of Iyappa is associated with the story of Vibhishana, the younger brother of the demon king Ravana. In Hindu mythology, Vibhishana sought the blessings of Shiva to atone for his actions during the war between the gods and demons. Shiva, in the form of Ayyappan, appeared before Vibhishana and granted him the boon of being a protector of the devotees at Sabarimala, who would be known as Iyappa.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Iyappa continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
